nodes.title: Belfius Green and Social Bonds
nodes.heading: 2.4.2.3 . Belfius Green and Social Bonds
nodes.start_phrase: Well aware of the crucial role played by the financial sector in ensuring a more sustainable future, Belfius aims to be meaningful and inspiring through its core businesses – not only for its customers, but also for the Belgian society as a whole.
nodes.summary:
- The section outlines Belfius Bank’s sustainability financing via Green and Social Bonds within its 2024 Annual Report.
- Frameworks:
  - Green Bond Framework (GBF) published in May 2021, aligned with ICMA Green Bond Principles.
  - Social Bond Framework (SBF) published in March 2024, aligned with ICMA Social Bond Principles.
  - Both frameworks reviewed by an independent Second Party Opinion provider; no specific issuance targets set.
- 2024 issuances:
  - EUR 750 million in Green Bonds to (re)finance eligible green loans and investments supporting a low-carbon, climate‑resilient transition.
  - EUR 575 million in Social Bonds to (re)finance eligible social loans and investments addressing social issues and promoting positive social outcomes, including for target populations.
- Reporting and assurance:
  - Annual allocation reports covering outstanding amounts, portfolio breakdown by eligible category, and any unallocated balances.
  - Impact reporting on key KPIs: environmental impact for Green Bonds and positive social impact for Social Bonds.
  - Reports subject to external Limited Assurance by an auditor.
- Governance:
  - A Green & Social Bond Committee oversees evaluation and selection of eligible assets and approves allocation and impact reports.
- Additional resources:
  - Full frameworks, eligible asset criteria, KPIs, annual reports, governance details, Second Party Opinion, and Limited Assurance Reports available at https://www.belfius.be/about-us/en/investors/debt-issuance/green-social-bonds.
- The next subsection (2.4.3 Meaningful Insurance) indicates that, following the DMA, material impacts, risks, and opportunities have been identified (details not included in this excerpt).

nodes.title: Meaningful Insurance
nodes.heading: 2.4.3. Meaningful Insurance
nodes.start_phrase: As a result of the DMA, the following Impacts, Risks and Opportunities have been identified as material:
nodes.summary:
- Belfius’ Green and Social Bond strategy:
  - Green Bond Framework (2021) aligned with ICMA Green Bond Principles; Social Bond Framework (2024) aligned with ICMA Social Bond Principles; both reviewed by an independent Second Party Opinion provider.
  - 2024 issuance: EUR 750 million in Green Bonds and EUR 575 million in Social Bonds; no specific issuance targets set.
  - Purpose: (re)finance eligible green and social assets, enhance transparency on environmental and social benefits.
  - Reporting: annual allocation and impact reports covering outstanding amounts, portfolio breakdown by category, unallocated proceeds, and KPIs on environmental and social outcomes; external Limited Assurance provided.
  - Governance: a Green & Social Bond Committee evaluates/ selects eligible assets and approves allocation and impact reports; detailed frameworks, eligible assets, KPIs, SPOs and assurance reports available on Belfius’ investor website.

- Meaningful Insurance: material impacts, risks and opportunities (downstream) identified via DMA:
  - Impacts: supporting climate transition and biodiversity; incentivizing adaptation; potential exposure to fossil-fuel activities, ecosystem destruction, human rights, and health and safety risks; promoting good working conditions.
  - Risks: mispricing non-life insurance for climate-related events; financial impacts from customer losses due to natural disasters.
  - Opportunities: new products for climate mitigation/adaptation and circular-economy solutions.

- Role of Belfius Insurance:
  - Non-life: protection against life hazards including climate-related catastrophes.
  - Life: addressing healthcare and pension needs to build societal resilience.
  - Investments: financing essential infrastructure; active engagement with investees, suppliers and customers to encourage sustainable behavior.

- Meaningful Insurance Journey and product lifecycle:
  - ESG embedded across product management and customer servicing; policies integrate climate change and biodiversity; circular economy viewed as a strategic opportunity.

- Product management and pricing:
  - Climate considerations integrated into property and mobility insurance; measurement of EU Taxonomy-aligned Green Non-Life Premium.
  - ESG integrated in product approval processes overseen by the Management Board; Product Oversight and Governance to ensure customer fit and value for money under IDD.
  - Pricing Policy Non-Life aligns with profitability, risk appetite and climate risk, with continuous monitoring and regulatory compliance.

- Mobility initiatives:
  - Three-pronged approach: avoid, reduce, replace emissions.
  - Products encouraging sustainable mobility: All Risk Bicycle Insurance (award-winning, comprehensive coverage) and Complementary Bicycle Assistance, promoting cycling adoption.

nodes.title: Meaningful Insurance - Introduction
nodes.heading: 2.4.3. Meaningful Insurance
nodes.start_phrase: As a result of the DMA, the following Impacts, Risks and Opportunities have been identified as material:
nodes.summary: This section introduces Belfius Insurance’s “Meaningful Insurance” topic, listing DMA-identified material Impacts, Risks and Opportunities focused on the downstream value chain. Impacts include developing insurance and (re)insurance that support the climate transition, climate adaptation, biodiversity, and good working conditions, alongside potential negative impacts from insuring fossil fuel-based energy, activities harming ecosystems, and sectors with elevated human rights or health and safety risks. Key risks are mispricing non-life products by not factoring climate events and financial losses from customers’ reduced value/profitability due to floods and other natural disasters. Opportunities include new revenue from products enabling climate mitigation/adaptation and circular economy (e.g., recycling). The section adds that non-life products protect against climate-related catastrophes, life insurance addresses healthcare and pensions to bolster a resilient Belgian society, investment activities advance essential infrastructure, and the company engages investees, suppliers, and customers to encourage sustainable behaviors.

nodes.title: Meaningful Insurance Journey
nodes.heading: 2.4.3.1 Meaningful Insurance Journey
nodes.start_phrase: To address current and future environmental and social challenges, Belfius Insurance encourages virtuous behaviour by incorporating environmental parameters into its product offerings throughout its product lifecycle.
nodes.summary:
- Belfius Insurance embeds ESG principles across the entire insurance journey, integrating key environmental challenges—especially climate change and biodiversity—into policies. While there is no standalone circular economy policy, it is seen as a strategic opportunity aligned with broader environmental goals.
- Product Management & Pricing: Products are tailored to protect clients from natural catastrophes and evolving environmental risks. Climate and environmental commitments are anchored in Belfius’ CEP, with measurement of EU Taxonomy–aligned non-life premiums (“Green Non-Life Premium”). ESG is integrated into the Approval Process Policy, overseen by the Management Board with multidisciplinary risk assessments. The Product Oversight and Governance Policy (under IDD, excluding large risks) ensures products meet customer needs, including sustainability objectives, and deliver value for money. The Non-Life Pricing Policy, approved by the Management Board, aligns with risk appetite including climate risk, and requires continuous pricing monitoring within regulatory guidelines.
- Mobility: A three-pronged decarbonization approach—avoid, reduce, replace—guides initiatives. Belfius facilitates shifts to sustainable mobility via a market-leading All Risk Bicycle Insurance (covering theft, damage, breakdowns, and flat batteries for non-motorized vehicles up to 25 km/h), awarded Decavi prizes in 2022, 2023, and 2024. Complementary bicycle assistance within personal assistance products encourages cycling as a sustainable transport mode.

nodes.title: Product Management & Pricing

nodes.start_phrase: Belfius Insurance aims to address the evolving needs of its clients, particularly in the face of increasing environmental challenges.
nodes.summary:
- Section from Belfius Bank’s 2024 Annual Report (Sustainability Statement) detailing Belfius Insurance’s “Meaningful Insurance Journey,” i.e., how ESG is embedded across the insurance product lifecycle—from product design and approval to pricing and customer service.

nodes.title: Product Management & Pricing - Introduction
nodes.heading: 2.4.3.1.1. Product Management & Pricing
nodes.start_phrase: Belfius Insurance aims to address the evolving needs of its clients, particularly in the face of increasing environmental challenges.
nodes.summary: Overview of Belfius Insurance’s Product Management & Pricing approach focused on environmental challenges and client protection against natural catastrophes. It links climate commitments to Belfius’ CEP, managing climate impacts on property and mobility insurance and measuring the share of non-life premiums aligned with EU Taxonomy climate adaptation objectives via the Green Non-Life Premium. ESG is embedded in the Approval Process Policy (overseen by the Management Board) with expert-led risk assessments for new or revised products to align with sustainability commitments. The Product Oversight and Governance Policy (Compliance accountable) applies to IDD-scope products except “large risks,” ensuring products fit customer characteristics, needs, and sustainability objectives and provide Value for Money. The Pricing Policy Non-Life (Management Board approved) ensures pricing within profitability limits and risk appetite including Climate Risk, with continuous monitoring, regulatory compliance, and adequate return on capital.

nodes.title: Mobility
nodes.heading: Mobility
nodes.start_phrase: In the domain of Mobility Belfius Insurance engages in initiatives that promote sustainable practices and behaviours.
nodes.summary:
- Focus and scope: Belfius Insurance embeds ESG principles across the full “insurance journey” (product management and pricing, underwriting, and servicing) to address environmental and social challenges, with climate change and biodiversity integrated into policies. Circular economy has no dedicated policy yet but is seen as a strategic opportunity.

- Product management and pricing:
  - Climate and Environment Policy (CEP) translates environmental commitments into insurance practices; measures EU Taxonomy–aligned Green Non‑Life Premium for climate adaptation.
  - ESG integrated into the Approval Process Policy for new/revised products, overseen by the Management Board, with multi-expert risk assessment.
  - Product Oversight and Governance (IDD scope; Compliance accountable) ensures products meet customer needs and sustainability objectives and deliver value for money.
  - Non‑Life Pricing Policy (Management Board–approved) aligns pricing with profitability, risk appetite, and climate risk, with ongoing monitoring and adjustment.

- Mobility initiatives:
  - All Risk Bicycle Insurance covering non‑motorized vehicles under 25 km/h (awarded 2022–2024) and complementary bicycle assistance.
  - Pay‑as‑you‑drive mileage insurance rewarding low annual mileage.
  - Up to 20% premium discounts for electric/less polluting vehicles.

- Property incentives:
  - 15% discount for new/fully renovated buildings (<10 years); additional 5% eco‑discount for EPC <150 kWh/m². In 2024, 39% of eligible new/renovated buildings received a total 20% premium reduction.

- Underwriting:
  - Board‑overseen Underwriting Policy ensures risks align with strategy and risk appetite; minimum standards and guidelines applied.
  - TAP applies to business clients with requirements on climate, biodiversity, and human rights; 100% of underwritten customers TAP‑compliant since 2022. Human Rights Policy complements these commitments.
  - Emphasis on societal role of non‑life insurance in covering catastrophes and unforeseen events.

- Servicing and claims:
  - Service practices aligned with CEP to strengthen relationships and environmental impact.
  - Proactive damage prevention using meteorological forecasts (six prevention advisories in 2024).
  - Enhanced client information for natural catastrophes to streamline claims.
  - MyBo digital tool as the preferred claims channel, especially during natural catastrophes.

nodes.title: Property
nodes.heading: Property
nodes.start_phrase: As for mobility, Belfius Insurance offers incentives that could encourage virtuous behaviours in the domain of property as well.
nodes.summary:
- Belfius Insurance promotes lower-emission mobility through a Pay-as-you-drive (Mileage Insurance) product with premiums based on anticipated annual mileage, and offers up to 20% premium discounts for clients switching to electric or less-polluting vehicles.
- In property insurance, it incentivizes energy-efficient buildings with a 15% discount for new or fully renovated buildings under 10 years old, plus an extra 5% eco-discount for EPC below 150 kWh/m²; in 2024, 39% of eligible new/renovated buildings received the full 20% “Green” reduction.
- Underwriting is governed by a Board-approved policy, Minimum Standards, and Guidelines to accept risks aligned with strategy and risk appetite; as a non-life insurer, Belfius provides protection against a wide range of catastrophes and unforeseen events.
- The firm applies its TAP to underwriting business clients, integrating criteria on climate change, biodiversity, and human rights; clients breaching TAP are excluded, and since 2022, 100% of underwritten customers are TAP-compliant; human rights commitments are further set out in a dedicated policy.
- Client servicing integrates sustainability and resilience, including proactive damage prevention using meteorological forecasts (six prevention advisories issued in 2024 for storms, thunderstorms, heatwaves), enhanced client information for natural catastrophe claims, and the MyBo digital tool as the preferred, streamlined channel for claims communication, especially during natural catastrophes.

nodes.title: Underwriting
nodes.heading: 2.4.3.1.2. Underwriting
nodes.start_phrase: Belfius Insurance’s underwriting process involves evaluating and selecting insurance risks for inclusion in its portfolio.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on Belfius Insurance’s sustainability-linked products and practices within the 2024 Annual Report.
- Mobility incentives to cut GHG emissions:
  - Pay-as-you-drive Mileage Insurance (since 2006) with premiums based on anticipated annual mileage.
  - Up to 20% premium discounts for customers switching to electric or lower-polluting vehicles, assessed via CO2 emissions and expected kilometers.
- Property incentives for energy efficiency:
  - 15% discount for owners of new or fully renovated buildings under 10 years old.
  - Additional 5% eco-discount for buildings with EPC below 150 kWh/m².
  - In 2024, 39% of eligible new/renovated buildings received the full 20% premium reduction.
- Underwriting policy and governance:
  - Board-overseen policy to identify, measure, and accept only risks aligned with strategy and risk appetite, supported by Minimum Standards and Underwriting Guidelines.
  - Emphasis on societal role of non-life insurance in covering catastrophes and unforeseen events.
  - Application of Belfius’ TAP to underwriting (covering climate, biodiversity, human rights); non-compliant clients are excluded; 100% TAP-compliant customer base since 2022.
  - Human Rights commitments also governed by a dedicated policy.
- Client servicing aligned with sustainability goals (CEP):
  - Proactive damage prevention using Royal Meteorological Institute forecasts; six prevention advisories issued in 2024 (storms, thunderstorms, heatwaves).
  - Enhanced client information and resources for natural catastrophes (e.g., floods, storms) to streamline claims.
  - Deployment of MyBo as the preferred digital channel for claims, especially during natural catastrophes, to improve efficiency and communication.

nodes.title: Servicing
nodes.heading: 2.4.3.1.3. Servicing
nodes.start_phrase: Servicing clients throughout the lifetime of their insurance contracts is a crucial aspect of maintaining a strong customer relationship.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on sustainability-driven insurance incentives and practices at Belfius Insurance across product design, underwriting, servicing, and reserve management.
- Mobility products: Pay-as-you-drive Mileage Insurance (since 2006) rewards low mileage with personalized premiums; up to 20% premium discounts for customers replacing conventional cars with electric or lower-emission vehicles (based on CO2 and expected kilometers).
- Property products: Incentives for energy-efficient buildings, including a 15% discount for new or fully renovated buildings under 10 years old and an additional 5% eco-discount for EPC under 150 kWh/m²; in 2024, 39% of eligible buildings received the full 20% “Green reduction.”
- Underwriting governance: Board-overseen policy to accept risks aligned with strategy and risk appetite; strong societal role in non-life coverage for catastrophes and unforeseen events; strict application of the Belfius TAP (climate, biodiversity, human rights) excluding non-compliant clients, with 100% TAP-compliant customer base since 2022; Human Rights Policy integration.
- Client servicing and sustainable claims handling:
  - Proactive damage prevention via meteorological forecasts, with six prevention advisories in 2024.
  - Clear client guidance for natural catastrophe claims.
  - MyBo digital tool as the preferred claims channel, especially during catastrophes.
  - Enhanced CatNat crisis plan updated in 2024 to handle successive small events creating large workloads.
  - Sustainable claims practices: compensation aligned to current building standards, repair-in-kind via Jaimy network, remote assessments through CED to cut travel, mobility budget option instead of replacement vehicles, and ESG criteria embedded in repairer agreements (sustainability labels required, reuse/quality-equivalent parts, greener replacement transport; persistent non-compliance can end partnerships).
  - Expanded coverages: no-cost coverage for energy-efficiency upgrades (solar panels, heat pumps, batteries, charging stations), liability for borrowed items in family insurance to support the sharing economy, and EV-specific support (boost charge for flat batteries; coverage for charging cables and accessories under (Mini-)Omnium).
- Reserve management (investments):
  - Portfolio composition addressed for corporate equities & bonds (26.46%, EUR 4.0bn of EUR 15.1bn) and real estate (5.40%, EUR 816m); mortgages managed at group level.
  - Threefold approach for corporate equities & bonds:
    1) Full TAP compliance achieved since 2022.
    2) ESG integration via the Investment Risk Framework (IRF) for all new investments since 2023, prioritizing companies transitioning in line with the Paris Agreement; by end-2024, 42% of listed investees have SBTi targets.
    3) Active ownership through engagement and proxy voting under an Engagement Policy aligned with UN SDGs and UNEP FI Principles for Sustainable Insurance; potential portfolio actions based on dialogue outcomes; Alco accountability for IRF and Engagement Policy.
  - Real estate investing guided by the IRF and Belfius Group’s Climate & Environment Policy (CEP), embedding sustainability considerations in new direct property investments.

nodes.title: Meaningful management of Belfius Insurance’s reserves
nodes.heading: 2.4.3.2. Meaningful management of Belfius Insurance’s reserves
nodes.start_phrase: The majority of Belfius Insurance’s reserves is invested in three categories namely: mortgages, corporate equities & bonds and real estate.
nodes.summary:
- EV customer support: Belfius Insurance offers breakdown assistance that includes a boost charge for flat EV batteries. Under its (Mini-) Omnium, charging cables and other accessories are covered against theft or damage, encouraging greener mobility.
- Management of insurance reserves: Majority allocated across mortgages, corporate equities & bonds, and real estate; this section details the latter two.
- Corporate equities & bonds (26.46% of portfolio; EUR 4.0bn of EUR 15.1bn):
  - TAP compliance: No investments in non-compliant companies/sectors; full portfolio compliance achieved since 2022.
  - ESG integration: Since 2023, ESG and Paris-aligned GHG reduction criteria embedded in the Investment Risk Framework (IRF), which sets operational limits (concentration, volatility, liquidity, credit quality). Alco accountable; applies to Belfius Insurance and fully consolidated subsidiaries. By end-2024, 42% of listed holdings had SBTi targets.
  - Active ownership: Engagement and proxy voting guided by an Engagement Policy aligned with UN SDGs and UNEP FI Principles for Sustainable Insurance; willingness to adjust positions based on ESG performance. Alco accountable.
- Real estate (5.40% of portfolio; EUR 816m): New direct property investments are guided by the IRF with sustainability considerations and by Belfius Group’s CEP.

nodes.title: Real estate
nodes.heading: 2.4.3.2.2. Real estate
nodes.start_phrase: At the end of 2024, 5.40% of Belfius Insurance’s investment portfolio (EUR 816 million of a total amount of EUR 15.1 billion) was invested in real estate.
nodes.summary:
- Context: Extract from Belfius Bank’s 2024 Annual Report (Sustainability Statement) detailing Belfius Insurance’s sustainability-focused products and investment management, plus an introduction to the EU Taxonomy.

- Customer offering for electric vehicles:
  - Breakdown assistance tailored to EVs, including boost charge for flat batteries.
  - Coverage under (Mini-) Omnium for charging cables and other accessories in case of theft or damage, supporting the shift to greener mobility.

- Management of Belfius Insurance’s reserves:
  - Reserves primarily invested across mortgages (managed at group level), corporate equities & bonds, and real estate.
  
- Corporate equities & bonds (26.46% of portfolio; EUR 4.0bn of EUR 15.1bn at end-2024):
  - Threefold process aligned to the UN SDGs:
    1) Compliance with Belfius’ TAP (sector/company exclusions). Full portfolio compliance achieved since 2022.
    2) ESG integration with a focus on Paris-aligned GHG reduction; criterion embedded in the Investment Risk Framework (IRF) for all new investments since 2023. IRF sets operational limits (concentration, volatility, liquidity, credit quality) and is overseen by ALCO; applies to Belfius Insurance and fully consolidated subsidiaries.
    3) Active engagement, including proxy voting, under an ALCO-accountable Engagement Policy aligned with the UN SDGs and UNEP FI PSI; willingness to adjust positions if misaligned with sustainability and ethical standards.
  - By end-2024, 42% of listed investees had SBTi targets to reduce carbon emissions.

- Real estate (5.40% of portfolio; EUR 816m of EUR 15.1bn at end-2024):
  - Governed by the IRF and guided by Belfius Group’s Climate & Environmental Policy (CEP).
  - Direct real estate strategy:
    - Focus on new/recent assets near major rail stations/mobility hubs to optimize energy performance and public transport access.
    - Example: January 2024 acquisition of a 10,000 m² BREEAM Very Good office in Mons; in 2024, two buildings rated BREEAM Very Good-equivalent and one Excellent-equivalent.
    - Portfolio GHG emissions calculated and a 2030 reduction target set; partnership with Sureal to conduct a comprehensive ESG analysis and action plan (energy performance, carbon reduction, social/governance improvements).
  - Decarbonized mobility:
    - Installation of 32 double EV charging stations at Alverberg Business Park (Hasselt), accessible to the public evenings/weekends; exploring further EV charging investments.
  - Biodiversity enhancements in line with CEP:
    - MC2 (Louvain-la-Neuve) green spaces awarded Natagora “Réseau Nature” label after an 18-month assessment; criteria include no pesticides, habitat preservation, native plants, encouraging wildlife diversity, and tackling invasive species. Monitoring continued in 2024, renewal expected 2025.
    - Extension of Natagora collaboration at Renouv’o (Mons) with plantings designed for biodiversity; inspection planned summer 2025 aiming for 2026 labeling.
    - Galilée property: agreement with co-owner INAMI to redevelop surroundings to promote and integrate biodiversity.

- EU Taxonomy (introduction):

nodes.title: Direct real estate
nodes.heading: Direct real estate
nodes.start_phrase: Direct real estate investments are mainly focused on new or recent properties within walking distance of major railway stations or mobility centres.
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines Belfius Insurance’s sustainability approach within its direct real estate portfolio and introduces the EU Taxonomy context.

- Direct real estate strategy: Prioritizes new or recent properties near major rail stations/mobility hubs to maximize energy efficiency and public transport access. Example: a 10,000 m² BREEAM Very Good–certified office acquired in Mons in January 2024. In 2024, two buildings achieved BREEAM “Very Good” equivalents and one “Excellent.” The company calculated GHG emissions for direct real estate and set a 2030 reduction target. With consultant Sureal, a portfolio-wide ESG analysis launched in 2024 to define actions on energy performance, carbon reduction, and social/governance improvements.

- Decarbonized mobility: Investment in EV charging infrastructure across the portfolio, including 32 double charging stations installed in 2024 at Alverberg Business Park (Hasselt), open to the public during evenings and weekends to encourage wider EV adoption. Further investments are under review to strengthen leadership in sustainable mobility.

- Biodiversity initiatives: Commitment to enhancing biodiversity as per the CEP. The MC2 site in Louvain-la-Neuve earned Natagora’s “Réseau Nature” label after an 18-month assessment, meeting criteria such as no chemical pesticides, habitat preservation, use of indigenous plants, support for wildlife diversity, and control of invasive species. Ongoing monitoring continues with anticipated label renewal in 2025. Collaboration with Natagora extends to the Renouv’o site in Mons (plantings completed Q1 2025; inspection summer 2025; target labeling in 2026). At the Galilée property, an agreement with co-owner INAMI will redevelop the surroundings to promote and integrate biodiversity.

- EU Taxonomy introduction: Provides context on the EU Sustainable Finance Action Plan (2018) and the EU Taxonomy as a transparency tool to channel capital to activities aligned with the European Green Deal. It defines a classification system for environmentally sustainable economic activities based on six environmental objectives.

nodes.title: Introduction
nodes.heading: 2.5.1. Introduction
nodes.start_phrase: In 2018, the European Commission released the Sustainable Finance Action Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Focus of direct real estate investments by Belfius Insurance on energy-efficient, recent buildings near public transport hubs; example: 10,000 m² BREEAM Very Good office acquisition in Mons (Jan 2024). Additional 2024 certifications: two buildings BREEAM “Very Good” equivalent and one “Excellent.”

- Introduction to the EU Taxonomy within the EU Sustainable Finance Action Plan and European Green Deal: framework for classifying environmentally sustainable economic activities across six environmental objectives (climate mitigation/adaptation, water/marine, circular economy, pollution prevention, biodiversity/ecosystems).

nodes.title: Introduction - Introduction
nodes.heading: 2.5.1. Introduction
nodes.start_phrase: In 2018, the European Commission released the Sustainable Finance Action Plan.
nodes.summary: Introduces the EU Taxonomy from the European Commission’s 2018 Sustainable Finance Action Plan, aligned with the European Green Deal, as a market transparency and classification tool to direct investment and compare sustainability performance of EU economic actors. It defines six environmental objectives—climate change mitigation, climate change adaptation, sustainable use and protection of water and marine resources, transition to a circular economy, pollution prevention and control, and protection and restoration of biodiversity and ecosystems—and sets eligibility criteria: substantial contribution to one objective, do no significant harm to the others per EU criteria, and adherence to minimum safeguards on human and labor rights, anti-bribery, taxation, and fair competition.

nodes.title: Disclosure obligation
nodes.heading: 2.5.1.1. Disclosure obligation
nodes.start_phrase: Article 8 of the EU Taxonomy Regulation imposes a disclosure obligation.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines the EU Taxonomy framework and its six environmental objectives: climate change mitigation and adaptation, water and marine resource protection, circular economy transition, pollution prevention, and biodiversity/ecosystem protection.
- Defines criteria for an environmentally sustainable economic activity: substantial contribution to one objective, do no significant harm to others, and compliance with minimum safeguards on human and labor rights, anti-bribery, taxation, and fair competition.
- Explains Article 8 disclosure obligations requiring in-scope entities to report how and to what extent their activities align with the EU Taxonomy, with KPIs specified in the Disclosure Delegated Act.
- Notes that disclosures have applied to NFRD entities since 2021 and will expand progressively under the CSRD from January 2025 to a broader set of companies.
- Describes “eligibility” (activities in scope of the taxonomy) and “alignment” (meeting technical screening criteria), introducing a sustainability accounting approach that evaluates turnover, CapEx, and OpEx to reflect both current performance and forward-looking environmental investments.
- Highlights additional, specific disclosure requirements for both financial and non-financial companies regarding involvement in nuclear and fossil gas activities to enhance market transparency.

nodes.title: Eligibility and alignment
nodes.heading: 2.5.1.2. Eligibility and alignment
nodes.start_phrase: The introduction of the EU Taxonomy enables companies to assess their sustainability performance by quantifying the proportion of their activities that are in the scope of the EU Taxonomy and that could therefore be considered as environmentally sustainable (the “ eligibility ”).
nodes.summary:
- Context: Excerpt from Belfius Bank’s 2024 Annual Report (Management Report – Sustainability Statement) detailing application of the EU Taxonomy.
- EU Taxonomy scope and objectives: Lists the six environmental objectives (climate mitigation, climate adaptation, water/marine resources, circular economy, pollution prevention, biodiversity/ecosystems).
- Criteria for environmentally sustainable activities: Must substantially contribute to one objective, do no significant harm to the others, and comply with minimum safeguards (human and labor rights, anti-bribery, taxation, fair competition).
- Disclosure obligations (Article 8): In-scope entities must report how and to what extent activities are linked to sustainable economic activities; NFRD entities have reported since 2021; CSRD will extend scope from January 2025; KPIs and formats are set by the Disclosure Delegated Act.
- Eligibility vs. alignment: Eligibility measures the share of activities within the Taxonomy’s scope; alignment assesses whether those activities meet EU technical screening criteria for environmental sustainability.
- Sustainability accounting approach: Goes beyond turnover to include CapEx and OpEx, indicating proactive efforts to improve environmental performance and long-term resilience.
- Nuclear and fossil gas activities: Both financial and non-financial companies must provide additional disclosures on involvement in six specified nuclear and fossil gas activities to enhance market transparency.

nodes.title: Nuclear and fossil gas related activities
nodes.heading: 2.5.1.3. Nuclear and fossil gas related activities
nodes.start_phrase: Both financial and non- financial companies are required to make additional specific disclosures relative to their involvement in nuclear and fossil gas activities.
nodes.summary: The excerpt outlines Belfius Bank’s EU Taxonomy approach within its 2024 Sustainability Statement. It explains the six EU environmental objectives and the criteria for an activity to be environmentally sustainable: substantial contribution to one objective, no significant harm to the others, and compliance with minimum safeguards on human rights, labor, anti-bribery, taxation, and competition. It details Article 8 disclosure obligations, noting the shift from NFRD to CSRD that broadens in-scope entities from 2025, and references the Disclosure Delegated Act that defines required KPIs and formats. It distinguishes Taxonomy eligibility (in-scope activities) from alignment (meeting technical screening criteria), and describes the sustainability accounting approach that assesses turnover, CapEx, and OpEx to capture both current performance and forward-looking investments. The text highlights specific disclosure requirements for nuclear and fossil gas-related activities (six defined categories) to enhance investor transparency. For scope, Belfius reports consolidated KPIs covering banking, insurance/reinsurance, asset management, and nuclear/gas activities, and also publishes a consolidated group KPI weighted by turnover shares. Strategically, Belfius uses the Taxonomy to identify climate solutions and financing opportunities, track its positive environmental contribution, and engage clients on improving alignment; it launched “Ambition Loans & Lease” that are Taxonomy-eligible (but not yet fully aligned) across real estate, mobility, transport, waste, and water. Finally, Belfius expands its reporting beyond the two climate objectives to, for the first time, disclose eligibility for the four remaining environmental objectives, informing future strategy integration.

nodes.title: Scope of Belfius’ EU Taxonomy disclosures
nodes.heading: 2.5.2. Scope of Belfius’ EU Taxonomy disclosures
nodes.start_phrase: As a large group, Belfius was previously required to publish a non -financial statement under the NFRD.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines EU Taxonomy disclosure requirements for nuclear and fossil gas activities, covering: pre-commercial advanced nuclear technologies; construction and safe operation of new nuclear plants; electricity generation from existing nuclear installations; electricity generation from fossil gaseous fuels; high-efficiency cogeneration from fossil gas; and production of heat/cool from fossil gas in efficient district systems. Purpose: enable investors to identify and avoid exposure to nuclear and gas activities if desired.
- Defines the scope of Belfius’ EU Taxonomy disclosures under CSRD (formerly NFRD), with consolidated KPIs for banking, insurance/reinsurance, asset management, and nuclear/gas-related activities, plus a group-level KPI computed as a turnover-weighted average of these segments.
- Describes Belfius’ strategy to use the EU Taxonomy to identify climate solutions and financing opportunities, track contributions to environmental objectives, launch Taxonomy-linked “Ambition Loans & Lease” (eligible but not yet fully aligned) across real estate, mobility, transport, waste and water, and engage clients to improve their Taxonomy alignment.
- Announces expanded disclosures: beyond prior reporting on climate objectives, Belfius now reports eligibility for exposures related to the four remaining environmental objectives, integrating these into strategy to reinforce sustainability commitments.

nodes.title: Belfius’ EU Taxonomy strategy
nodes.heading: 2.5.3. Belfius’ EU Taxonomy strategy
nodes.start_phrase: So far, Belfius has used the EU Taxonomy as a means to identify climate solutions and financing opportunities , and in particular as a metric enabling the group to better track its contribution to financing assets that are making a positive contribution to environmental objectives.
nodes.summary:
- Clarifies EU Taxonomy disclosure on nuclear and fossil gas activities, listing covered categories (pre‑commercial advanced nuclear, new nuclear construction/operation, existing nuclear generation, fossil gas electricity, high‑efficiency fossil gas cogeneration, and efficient district heating/cooling from fossil gas) to enable investor choice and exclusion.

- Details consolidated KPIs reported for: banking (Belfius Bank), insurance/reinsurance (Belfius Insurance), asset management (Belfius AM), and nuclear/gas-related activities.
- Describes a group‑level consolidated KPI calculated as a weighted average of segment KPIs based on each activity’s share of total consolidated turnover, aiding investor and creditor use.

- Introduces “Ambition Loans & Lease” (since 2022) as Taxonomy‑eligible products for real estate, mobility, transport, waste and water; notes they are not yet fully Taxonomy‑aligned against technical screening criteria.

nodes.title: Belfius’ EU Taxonomy disclosures
nodes.heading: 2.5.4. Belfius’ EU Taxonomy disclosures
nodes.start_phrase: After reporting on the eligibility and alignment of its exposures under the EU Taxonomy’s two climate objectives, Belfius is, for the first time, reporting on the eligibility of its exposures to the four remaining environmental objectives.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines EU Taxonomy-specific disclosures for nuclear and fossil gas, detailing six activity categories (advanced nuclear technologies; construction/operation of new nuclear plants; electricity generation from existing nuclear; electricity from fossil gas; high-efficiency cogeneration from fossil gas; and heat/cool from fossil gas in efficient district systems) to help investors screen exposure to these sectors.

- Explains the 2024 disclosure approach: first-time eligibility reporting for the four environmental objectives beyond climate; reliance on client/investee data via ESG providers; conservative methodology leading to 0% alignment where technical screening evidence is unavailable; strong emphasis on transparency and avoidance of double counting; disclosures organized by business segment with full templates in the appendix.
- Details Belfius Bank’s reporting as a credit institution (prudential consolidation per CRR 575/2013) and its main KPI, the Green Asset Ratio (GAR), presented for stock (as of 31/12/2023) and flow (2024 new production), plus views on financial guarantees and assets under management:
  - GAR (stock): 0.12% (turnover-based) and 0.15% (CapEx-based); coverage 78.59%; assets excluded from GAR numerator 41.31%; from denominator 21.41%.
  - GAR (flow): 0.08% (turnover-based) and 0.09% (CapEx-based).
  - Financial guarantees: 6.80% (turnover-based) and 12.30% (CapEx-based).
  - Assets under management: 0.01% (turnover-based) and 0.16% (CapEx-based).

nodes.title: Belfius’ EU Taxonomy disclosures - Introduction
nodes.heading: 2.5.4. Belfius’ EU Taxonomy disclosures
nodes.start_phrase: After reporting on the eligibility and alignment of its exposures under the EU Taxonomy’s two climate objectives, Belfius is, for the first time, reporting on the eligibility of its exposures to the four remaining environmental objectives.
nodes.summary: Introduction to Belfius’ 2024 EU Taxonomy disclosures, noting prior reporting on eligibility/alignment for the two climate objectives and, for the first time, eligibility of exposures for the four remaining environmental objectives. Explains methodology: reliance on latest EU Taxonomy data from clients and investees, collaboration with specialized ESG data providers, cautious approach often resulting in 0% alignment where compliance with technical screening criteria under the Disclosure Delegated Act and latest European Commission interpretations cannot be evidenced. Emphasizes transparency about data gaps, prevention of double counting, and presentation of results by business segments (banking, insurance and reinsurance, asset management), with full mandatory reporting templates provided in the Appendix.

nodes.title: Belfius as a credit institution
nodes.heading: 2.5.4.1. Belfius as a credit institution
nodes.start_phrase: As a credit institution, Belfius Bank’s EU Taxonomy disclosure is based on the scope of its prudential consolidation determined in accordance with Regulation (EU) 575/2013 of the European Parliament and Council.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and approach: Belfius prepares EU Taxonomy disclosures using the latest client/investee data, supported by ESG data providers. It applies a cautious, evidence-based methodology, often reporting 0% alignment where required information or proof of compliance with technical screening criteria is unavailable, and takes steps to avoid double counting. Disclosures are structured by business segment (banking, insurance/reinsurance, asset management), with full templates in the appendix.

- Banking (credit institution):
  - Main KPI: Green Asset Ratio (GAR), calculated on the prudential consolidation scope (CRR 575/2013), showing the share of Taxonomy-aligned assets in the banking book.
  - 2024 results:
    - GAR on stock: 0.12% (turnover), 0.15% (CapEx); coverage 78.59%; assets excluded from numerator 41.31%; assets excluded from denominator 21.41%.
    - GAR on flow (new production): 0.08% (turnover), 0.09% (CapEx).
    - Financial guarantees: 6.80% (turnover), 12.30% (CapEx).
    - Assets under management: 0.01% (turnover), 0.16% (CapEx).
  - Key limitations: GAR numerator excludes exposures to companies not subject to NFRD, while the denominator includes them, disadvantaging banks with such exposures; limited asset coverage further constrains comparability.
  - Composition and drivers:
    - Focus on NFRD-reporting large companies in sectors like electricity transmission and electrical equipment manufacturing—only 4% of total assets.
    - Residential mortgages to households represent 25% of assets; reported at 0% alignment due to complexity and lack of verifiable evidence to meet criteria (including DNSH for climate adaptation).
    - 21% of assets excluded (trading book; exposures to central governments, central banks, supranationals—including Belgian regions).
    - 41% of assets relate to counterparties (e.g., non-EU, non-listed large companies, SMEs) defaulting to 0% alignment under current rules.
  - Next steps: Enhance data strategy and collection, raise client awareness on sustainable financing, and engage sector-wide. Belfius recommends reading GAR alongside broader ESG Pillar III disclosures (e.g., BTAR and climate change mitigating actions) for a fuller view.

- Insurance and reinsurance:
  - Two KPIs: an underwriting KPI (actual contribution of underwriting to climate change adaptation) and an investment KPI (investment portfolio’s contribution to climate objectives).
  - Underwriting scope: EU Taxonomy currently applies to climate change adaptation for non-life insurance/reinsurance covering climate-related perils (e.g., hail, windstorms). Relevant Belfius lines: motor “omnium” and property; 12.13% of total premiums relate to climate-related peril coverage.
  - Alignment assessment: Requires meeting five tiers (climate risk modelling/pricing leadership, product design, innovative coverage, data sharing, post-disaster service). Belfius Insurance reports 0% alignment currently due to not yet having a forward-looking pricing model; it is awaiting clearer guidance on time horizons and scenario integration.

- Transparency note on mortgages: As a retail lender, Belfius reports 0% Taxonomy alignment for its mortgage portfolio in the absence of verified DNSH compliance for climate adaptation, to avoid overstating the GAR.

nodes.title: Belfius as an (re)insurer
nodes.heading: 2.5.4.2. Belfius as an (re)insurer
nodes.start_phrase: The contribution of Belfius Insurance to the EU’s environmental objectives is expressed by two key metrics:
nodes.summary:
- Focus: EU Taxonomy reporting for Belfius as (re)insurer and as asset manager, with related implications for the bank’s mortgage portfolio.
- Underwriting KPI (Belfius Insurance):
  - EU Taxonomy covers non-life insurance/reinsurance for climate change adaptation only, assessing how products help policyholders manage climate-related perils (e.g., hail, windstorms).
  - Relevant business lines: other motor (omnium) and fire/property; premiums covering climate perils represent 12.13% of total consolidated premiums.
  - Alignment criteria span five tiers: climate risk modelling/pricing, product design, innovative coverage, data sharing, and post-disaster services.
  - Reported alignment is 0% due to the absence of a forward-looking pricing model; uncertainty over time horizons and sector-wide interpretation drives a cautious approach pending further guidance.
- Bank mortgage portfolio:
  - Reported 0% alignment for mortgages due to lack of verified “Do No Significant Harm” (DNSH) to the climate adaptation objective, to avoid overstating the Green Asset Ratio (GAR).
- Investment KPI / Green Investment Ratio (GIR) for Belfius Insurance:
  - Turnover-aligned: 0.82% (EUR 113m); CapEx-aligned: 1.24% (EUR 171m).
  - Coverage ratio: 68.49% of investments (EUR 14bn) excluding sovereigns.
  - Portfolio characteristics shaping low alignment:
    - Liability-driven, buy-and-hold strategy with significant sovereign holdings (30%) excluded from GIR.
    - Low exposure to NFRD-reporting companies (7%).
    - “Other counterparties and assets” (23%) include mortgages and direct real estate; DNSH hurdles for mortgages persist.
    - Active work underway to improve Taxonomy alignment of directly held real estate with external consultancy support.
    - Unit-linked (Branche 23) exposures (22%) face data availability challenges for Taxonomy assessment.
- Belfius Asset Management (Belfius AM) GIR:
  - Turnover-aligned: 0.92% (EUR 331m); CapEx-aligned: 1.26% (EUR 457m).
  - Coverage ratio: 99.48% (EUR 36bn) excluding sovereigns.
  - Exposure to NFRD-reporting companies is modest (12%) but higher than for Belfius Bank and Belfius Insurance.

nodes.title: Belfius as an asset manager
nodes.heading: 2.5.4.3. Belfius as an asset manager
nodes.start_phrase: The following chart provides an overview of Belfius AM’s Green Investment Ratio (GIR) .
nodes.summary:
- Presents Investment KPIs focused on the EU Taxonomy Green Investment Ratio (GIR) for Belfius Insurance and Belfius Asset Management (Belfius AM), explaining GIR as the weighted share of investments associated with taxonomy-aligned activities within covered assets under management (excluding sovereigns).

- Key taxonomy data challenges for Belfius Insurance: meeting “Do No Significant Harm” criteria for mortgages; limited EU Taxonomy data for 22% of investments held in unit-linked life contracts (Branche 23); ongoing work with a consultancy to improve taxonomy alignment of direct real estate.
- Belfius AM GIR results: 0.92% turnover-based (EUR 331m) and 1.26% CapEx-based (EUR 457m); coverage ratio 99.48% with EUR 36bn of assets covered.
- Belfius AM exposure characteristics: 12% to NFRD-reporting companies; 79% in “other counterparties and assets,” mainly external investment funds with limited look-through and scarce EU Taxonomy data; overall taxonomy-aligned percentages similar to Belfius Insurance.
- Social information – Own workforce: Belfius underscores employees’ central role in strategy and service quality, committing to good working conditions (pay, healthcare, freedom of association) and leveraging innovation and AI to enhance service quality and the work environment.

nodes.title: Social information
nodes.heading: 3. Social information
nodes.start_phrase: Belfius mission to be “Meaningful and inspiring for Belgian Society. Together” includes the preface that employees have an essential role in the success of the strategy and operations.
nodes.summary:
- Context: Sustainability Statement, Social information – Own workforce, Belfius Bank Annual Report 2024.
- Employee focus: Belfius’ mission emphasizes employees’ essential role in strategy and operations, aiming to offer good working conditions (appropriate pay, access to healthcare, freedom of association) to attract and retain talent, ensure service quality, and support customer satisfaction and loyalty alongside financial results.
- Innovation and AI: Ongoing innovation and workplace digitalization, including use of AI, are highlighted as avenues to improve service quality, work environment, and employee performance.

- Non-employee workers: Belfius also works with contractors, third parties, temporary workers, and trainees, who are treated equally to internal employees under the wellbeing law, with the same rights and obligations.

- Headcount evolution by contract type and gender:

structure.title: Social information
structure.heading: III. Social information
structure.start_phrase: Belfius mission to be “Meaningful and inspiring for Belgian Society. Together” includes the preface that employees have an essential role in the success of the strategy and operations.
structure.summary:
- Scope and context
  - Sustainability Statement sections summarizing Social information (own workforce), Workers in the value chain (human rights), Consumers and end-users (customer protection, privacy, security, inclusion), Community involvement, and a lead-in to Governance/Business Conduct.
  - Double Materiality Assessment (DMA) identifies material Impacts, Risks and Opportunities for own workforce, customer transparency, information security/data protection, financial inclusion, innovation and digitalization, community involvement, and governance.

- 3.1 Own workforce
  - Workforce profile (31/12/2024): 7,198 employees (99% permanent; 86% full-time); average FTE 6,767; phase-in on S1-7 (non-employees) and S1-12 (persons with disabilities). Contractors/temps/trainees treated equally under wellbeing law.

  - Material IROs (own operations): impact from providing good working conditions; risk of talent attraction/retention affecting service quality and revenue; opportunity from innovation/digitalization to improve performance.

- 3.1.1 Labor practices and human rights
  - Human Rights Policy and Code of Conduct; Management Board responsible for implementation.
  - Formal prohibition of child/forced labor; respect for freedom of association and collective bargaining (94.6% covered); all sites with worker representation.
  - Anti-discrimination and zero-tolerance for violence/harassment; grievance mechanisms with internal and external procedures; applies to all staff, externals, and governance bodies.
  - GDPR compliance for employee data privacy.
  - Gender-neutral, non-discriminatory remuneration; equal access to part-time; broad social protection and enhanced insurance benefits.
  - Pay metrics: unadjusted gender pay gap 11% (monthly salary basis); total remuneration ratio 13.4:1 (highest paid vs median).

- 3.1.2 Health & well-being
  - Health & Safety Policy aligned with Belgian Wellbeing Law; dynamic risk management across seven wellbeing domains; prevention advisers (including psychosocial) and Committee for Prevention and Protection at Work (10 Bank, 12 Insurance meetings in 2024).
  - Annual job risk analyses; right to report/suspend unsafe work; contractors covered similarly; root-cause analysis for incidents.
  - Key risks: psychosocial and ergonomic for staff; contractor risks managed via active contractor management; no serious industrial accidents with contractors.
  - Training and awareness: mandatory H&S e-learning, evacuation drills; optional stress and AED trainings; aggression management for client-facing roles.
  - Support services: internal psychosocial team; 24/7 confidential Employee Assistance Program (193 cases for 133 employees in 2024); external prevention service IDEWE (~1,800 hours/year); periodic medical check-ups.
  - 2024 metrics: 100% covered by H&S management system; fatalities 0; recordable accident rate 1.69% (19 accidents); days lost 95.
  - Remediation pathways: internal informal/formal psychosocial procedures; external inspection recourse; whistleblowing channel; no human rights incidents resulting in penalties.

- 3.1.3 Talent management
  - Recruitment: 1,188 vacancies opened; 40 Young Professionals; 84 trainees; stronger employer branding (STEM, tech, private/wealth), participation in >46 job fairs; unified onboarding incl. subsidiaries; dedicated internal mobility support.
  - Turnover: departures rose to 428 (2024), largely retirees (44%); churn 6.1% (2024) vs 5.3% (2023).
  - Learning & Development: structured offerings via MyDevelopment (foundations, on-demand, invitation-only); performance/career reviews for 24.3% in 2024 (tool “Talent=Hub” launched Nov 2024 to scale in 2025); average training days 5.1 (5.0 female; 5.3 male); emphasis on continuous feedback and internal mobility.

- 3.1.4 Diversity & inclusion (DEI)
  - DEI embedded via Diversity Manager and Steering Group: women in management quotas, women in STEM, generational diversity; bias reduction in recruitment; Inclusive Panels Charter; Women in Finance participation; Amsterdam Charter signed; Diversity Room launched.
  - Gender in management (2024): women managers 40.9%; women key execs 41.7%; women senior execs 47.8%. Public tracking shows 43.5% women in management vs 44% target by 2025 (reported to Board/Management twice yearly).
  - Work-life balance: flexible telework (up to 3 days), part-time options, leave policies; family-related leave uptake 10% overall (13% female; 8% male).
  - Belfius Young Community supports <36 employees with events, BoD Q&A, and innovation brainstorming.

- 3.1.5 Employee satisfaction and engagement
  - Annual engagement survey for all entities; anonymous; high response rates.
  - 2024 results: satisfaction Bank 91.7%, Insurance 92.3%, Group 91.7%; engagement Bank 85.8%, Insurance 85.2%, Group 85.8%. Management Board owns execution/follow-up.

- 3.1.6 Innovation & digitalization (employees)
  - Focus on empowering employees with AI and modern tools; no centralized targets yet.
  - Internal ChatGPT; Microsoft Copilot pilot for 300 employees (with training/support).
  - Strategic moves: investment in Mistral AI (Series B); partnership with Alan on AI-driven mental health/absenteeism solutions.
  - Digital workplace modernization: platform migration, new eco-friendly laptops, hybrid-ready meeting rooms.
  - Inclusive digital talent initiatives: partnerships with BeCode, Passwerk, and ‘S.He Goes Digital’ program.

- 3.2 Workers in the value chain: human rights
  - Group-wide Human Rights Policy aligned with ILO principles; signatory to UN Global Compact, UNEP FI PRB/PSI, UN PRI.
  - Risk mapping highlights construction (highest), plus real estate, tech manufacturing, retail, power/equipment as risk sectors.
  - TAP (exclusionary) policy enforces UNGC labor principles in portfolios; Supplier Code of Conduct aligns to UNGC for upstream workers.
  - Governance via ESG, procurement, legal, communications; whistleblowing open to all parties; no human rights incidents or remediation cases in 2024.

- 3.3 Consumers & end-users
  - Customer orientation central to mission; adherence to sector codes (Febelfin, Assuralia, BEAMA) and EU regulations (MiFID II, IDD, AML/C DD).
  - Material IROs cover customer transparency, information security/data protection, financial inclusion, and innovation/digitalization risks and opportunities.

- 3.3.1 Innovation & digitalization: customer interaction
  - Re=Bel platform enables theme-based investing (e.g., renewable energy, mobility, inclusion).
  - 2024 redesign of Belfius Mobile App: more intuitive, Smart Search, Feature Discovery, accessibility features (speech output, subtitles, reduced animations), greener access to data without login.
  - “Always On” engagement: smart assistant, rapid call-back, quick in-person appointments; non-digital options via cashless machines and phone banking.
  - Belfius E-sign with itsme; fully digital onboarding for individuals and businesses.
  - Anti-phishing program integrated in app (card limits, data confirmation).
  - Societal innovation support: Quantum Circle, UGent Racing Team, Academic Chair in Ethics & AI, and Jaimy platform.

- 3.3.2 Data protection
  - Public Privacy Charter; internal Privacy Risk Policy and risk-based framework aligned to GDPR; Board and committees oversee; quarterly Privacy Steering Committee.
  - Comprehensive GDPR processes: privacy register, DPIAs, cookie policy, international transfer rulings, DPO/CISO/DSO/CDO/NFR/Legal/Compliance/Procurement roles.
  - Third-party privacy assessments embedded in TPRM; full rollout planned for 2025.
  - Targets and monitoring via KRIs and risk appetite; event-based breach and DSAR handling.
  - 2024 results: zero overdue supervisory notifications; 9 DPA notifications (Q1:4, Q2:3, Q3:1, Q4:1; target <5/quarter met); zero late DSAR responses.

- 3.3.3 Information security
  - Three Lines of Defence with DSO (1st), CISO/NFR (2nd), Audit (3rd); quarterly Board committee reporting; ISMS and Risk Appetite with KRIs and remediation planning.
  - Information Security Steering chaired by CRO/CTO; Technology Committee advises on IT/digital/security.
  - Compliance with GDPR, PSD2, DORA, NIS; frequent internal/external/regulatory audits.
  - Biennial external maturity assessment (target >3 achieved); annual red teams, pentests, scanning, config reviews; cyber hygiene checks; dedicated security roadmap and budget.
  - Workforce awareness: mandatory trainings, monthly phishing simulations; onboarding training; reporting of completion and click rates to ISS.
  - 24/7 external SOC monitoring; tested incident response and crisis management; third-party incident handling; active threat intelligence.
  - Collaboration with sector bodies (Febelfin, Belgian Cyber Security Coalition, FS-ISAC).

- 3.3.4 Financial inclusion & access to finance
  - Basic banking service: 61,000 basic accounts (49% market share); collaboration with social organizations; 163,303 social accounts active (end 2024).
  - Branch accessibility: more walk-in availability (“Always On”); easy digital appointment booking.
  - Cash access: Batopin network deployed to 581 sites (1,459 machines) by end 2024; 410 branch cashless machines maintained; special support for 70+ (manual transfers, paper statements).
  - Non-digital access: Universal Account; phone banking (1,173,683 calls in 2024); Walloon info sessions with Febelfin; “CYBERSMART” anti-fraud campaign (incl. paper formats).
  - Accessibility for disabilities: blind notch debit cards, braille statements; accessible recyclers and Bancontact CASH points with audio/braille; guided cashless machines in all branches by H1 2025; aiming for WCAG 2.2 AA.
  - Inclusive financing for women entrepreneurs: client base stats (e.g., 37% self-employed are women; strong share in liberal professions and startups); signed Febelfin Charter; partnerships/events (WOW/“Money Talks”, High Her, Womenpreneur).

- 3.3.5 Customer satisfaction
  - Target 95% satisfaction; 2024 survey to 519k+ customers; overall score 94%; results used by business lines; overseen by Head of Customer Research.

- 3.3.6 Complaint management
  - Formal Complaints Policy (MiFID/FSMA-compliant) with multi-level handling (branches/bankers; Complaints depts; Belfius Negotiator; Federal Ombudsman/Court); comprehensive reporting to management and audit bodies.
  - 2024: 13,530 complaints (+1% YoY), incl. discrimination (88; up 159%, drivers include accessibility of devices, unaccompanied minor account processes, and perceived bias) and privacy (434; up 82%, mainly due to Maestro replacement campaign).
  - No severe human rights-related complaints requiring formal remediation.

- 3.4 Community involvement
  - Material IROs emphasize positive societal impact, reputation, and product co-design through engagement.
  - Governance via Brand Committee and Reputation Risk Policy; focus on durable partnerships with impactful organizations.
  - Key initiatives and 2024 amounts: Viva for Life (€816k), Télévie (€75k), JEZ! (€390k); Special Olympics Belgium (main partner); Campus 19 sponsorship; STEM outreach (Da’s Geniaal!/C’est génial!).
  - Philanthropy through impact investments: since 2019, €11.4m donated to charities (e.g., Stichting Tegen Kanker, Airscan, KBF projects, Close the Gap, Tubbe, Responsible Young Drivers, Campus 19, Natagora/Natuurpunt).
  - Beats customers’ directed giving: €500k in 2024 (health, planet, people via JEZ!/Viva for Life).
  - Access to art: Belfius Art Collection (>4,000 works); loans to museums; public Belfius Art Gallery (curated selections, inclusive guided tours for visually impaired).

- 4 Governance information (intro)
  - As a Belgian systemic bank and insurer, Belfius outlines governance areas on Business Conduct, Sustainable Procurement, and Resilience & Compliance.
  - Material IROs include risks linked to corporate governance/business conduct, sustainable procurement impacts on environment and labor, and resilience/compliance with regulatory expectations.
  - 4.1 Business Conduct opens with emphasis on ethics, integrity, and compliance as foundations for resilience and stakeholder trust (framework details to follow).

structure.title: Governance information
structure.heading: IV. Governance information
structure.start_phrase:
As a Belgian systemic bank and insurance company, Belfius needs to comply with applicable laws and regulations 
and act in accordance with the highest standards of integrity in all its operations and activities.
structure.summary:
- Focus and scope: Governance information for a Belgian systemic bank-insurer, covering Business Conduct, Sustainable Procurement, and Resilience & Compliance, with material impacts/risks identified via the DMA for own operations and upstream value chain.

- Business Conduct and Compliance Framework:
  - Comprehensive policy suite: Compliance Charter (independent function per NBB/FSMA circular), Integrity Policy, Code of Conduct, and topic-specific policies on market abuse, anti-bribery, anti-fraud, AML/CFT, and whistleblowing.
  - Whistleblowing channels open to employees and external stakeholders with protections per EU Directive 2019/1937; Compliance evaluates all reports.

- Corporate culture and training:
  - Mandatory onboarding and periodic e-learning on Code of Ethics, anti-corruption, whistleblowing, GDPR, and market abuse; ad hoc classroom deep-dives for exposed departments.
  - 2024 emphasis on market abuse training for higher-risk functions.
  - Training coverage/frequency highlights: anti-bribery 89% of all employees (every 5 years); market abuse 100% of risk functions and 89% of all employees (every 5 years); AML 89% for both (every 2 years).

- Detection, monitoring, and 2024 outcomes:
  - Independent investigations by Compliance/Audit; regular reporting to governance bodies; IT controls monitor atypical transactions.
  - No whistleblowing cases reported in 2024; no convictions or fines for anti-corruption/anti-bribery violations.

- Sustainable Procurement:
  - Policies: Supplier Code of Conduct (aligned with UN Global Compact), General Terms & Conditions of Purchase, and Procurement Policy (roles, process, ESG integration, conflict of interest, anti-bribery).
  - ESG integration in sourcing: sustainability weighted at 10% in RFP scoring for new key suppliers; procurement team trained on sustainable procurement.
  - Use of EcoVadis to assess suppliers across Environment, Labour & Human Rights, Ethics, and Sustainable Procurement based on international standards (GRI, SDGs, OECD, ISO).
  - 2024 performance: 80% of supplier spend assessed by EcoVadis; ESG due diligence on 100% of new critical suppliers; 80% of existing critical suppliers with valid EcoVadis scorecards.
  - Forward targets: 100% of critical suppliers ESG screened; 80% of total third-party spend ESG screened; all third parties sign the Code of Conduct; remediation support offered where scores are insufficient.

- Resilience & Compliance (prudential strength and risk governance):
  - Alignment with Basel III and Solvency II; internal targets: CET1 ≥13.5% (group), Solvency II ≥160% (after dividend).
  - Reported positions (2024): CET1 15.39% (req. 10.931%), Total Capital 18.62% (req. 7%), Leverage 6.46% (req. 3%), NSFR 133% (req. 100%), LCR 139% (req. 100%), Solvency II 196% (target 160%).
  - Group-wide integrated risk management: consistent policies/tools across entities, Risk Appetite Framework (quantitative KRIs and qualitative statements), ICAAP/ORSA, internal control reporting; RAF updated and approved Dec 2024.
  - Stress testing: annual ICAAP stress tests with 2025–2027 scenarios (high inflation/geopolitical tensions; hard landing from US tariffs), second-round effects and solvency-liquidity feedback loop; reverse stress tests including external fraud; results confirm resilience.
  - Climate risk: participation in ECB/EBA exercises and internal climate stress tests; impacts significant but manageable.
  - Recovery plan: governance, activation procedures, and measures to restore viability under severe stress submitted to ECB.
  - Resolution: ongoing cooperation with SRB; noted progress on data quality, completeness, and timeliness; further resolvability enhancements planned.

- External assurance:
  - Statutory auditor performed a limited assurance engagement (first year) on consolidated sustainability information for year ended 31 Dec 2024.
  - Conclusion: nothing has come to attention indicating non-compliance with Belgian law (art. 3:32/2), ESRS, the group’s identification process, or EU Taxonomy art. 8.
  - Engagement conducted under ISAE 3000 (Revised) and ISQM 1; independence and quality management requirements observed.

structure.title: Auditor’s limited assurance report
structure.heading: V. Auditor’s limited assurance report
structure.start_phrase:
In the context of the legal limited assurance engagement on the consolidated sustainability information of Belfius 
Bank NV/SA (“the Company”) and its subsidiaries (jointly “the Group”), we provide you with our report on this 
engagement.
structure.summary:
- Statutory auditor’s limited assurance report on Belfius Bank NV/SA’s consolidated sustainability information for the year ended 31 December 2024, addressed to the General Meeting.
- Engagement and mandate: appointed on 19 March 2025 (following board proposal, audit committee recommendation, and workers’ council presentation); engagement letter dated 15 October 2024 (before Belgian transposition of EU Directive 2022/2464); mandate runs until the meeting approving the 2025 annual accounts; first year of assurance.
- Limited assurance conclusion: nothing came to the auditor’s attention indicating that the sustainability information is not, in all material respects, prepared in line with Article 3:32/2 of the Belgian Companies’ and Associations’ Code and ESRS, inconsistent with the Group’s defined Process for identifying sustainability information (as disclosed in the report), or non‑compliant with Article 8 of the EU Taxonomy Regulation for the environmental disclosures (section 2.5 EU Taxonomy).
- Basis for conclusion: engagement performed under ISAE 3000 (Revised) as adopted in Belgium; compliance with relevant ethical and independence requirements; firm operates under ISQM 1; sufficient appropriate evidence obtained; scope excludes comparative figures.
- Board of directors’ responsibilities: design and disclosure of the Process (double materiality), stakeholder understanding, identification and materiality assessment of impacts/risks/opportunities, preparation in line with ESRS and EU Taxonomy Article 8, establishment of internal controls, and use of appropriate methods, assumptions and estimates; audit committee oversight of sustainability reporting.
- Inherent limitations: forward‑looking information prepared under ESRS is based on assumptions; actual outcomes may differ materially.
- Auditor’s responsibilities: obtain limited assurance (not reasonable assurance) on freedom from material misstatement due to fraud or error; understand and evaluate consistency of the Process with its description; understand control environment and reporting processes; identify areas prone to material misstatement; design focused procedures recognizing higher fraud detection risk.
- Summary of work performed: inquiries and review of internal documentation on the Process (including sources like stakeholder engagement and strategy documents); evaluation of consistency with the disclosed Process (double materiality); assessment of inclusion of material information; evaluation of structure/presentation against ESRS; inquiries, analytics, and limited‑sample substantive procedures on selected disclosures; assessment of methods for estimates and forward‑looking information; understanding of EU Taxonomy eligibility/alignment identification and related disclosures.
- Independence and compatibility: auditor and network performed no incompatible engagements and remained statutory auditor throughout the mandate.
- Report details: issued in Zaventem on 26 March 2025 by KPMG Bedrijfsrevisoren/Réviseurs d’Entreprises, represented by Olivier Macq.
- Appendix reference: index table of ESRS 2 disclosure requirements and related datapoints (including those from other EU legislation) with document placement.

nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: Appendix of Belfius Bank’s 2024 Sustainability Statement mapping all ESRS disclosure requirements (including data points from other EU legislation per ESRS 2 Appendix B) to where they appear in the report, and presenting mandatory EU Taxonomy disclosures.

- ESRS index and materiality mapping:
  - ESRS 2 (General): Basis of preparation; disclosures for specific circumstances; governance roles and diversity; ESG oversight and incentive schemes; due diligence statement; risk management and internal controls; strategy, business model and value chain; stakeholder interests; material impacts/risks/opportunities (IRO) and processes.
  - Climate (E1): Transition plan; policies, actions, targets (incl. GHG reduction targets); energy consumption and mix (incl. fossil sources and intensity for high-impact sectors); Scope 1, 2, 3 and total GHG emissions and intensity; GHG removals/credits; anticipated financial effects of physical and transition risks and opportunities; EU Taxonomy minimum disclosure. Specifics include disaggregation by acute/chronic physical risk, asset locations at physical risk, and energy-efficiency classes of real estate.
  - Other environmental topics marked not material with minimum disclosures as applicable:
    - E2 (Pollution) – Pollution of air, water, soil and E-PRTR pollutants.
    - E3 (Water and marine resources) – Policies, water consumption, recycling/reuse.
    - E4 (Biodiversity and ecosystems) – Strategy/IRO references; policies on land, oceans, deforestation.
    - E5 (Resource use and circular economy) – Resource outflows, non-recycled and hazardous/radioactive waste.
  - Social:
    - S1 (Own workforce): Policies (human rights, anti-trafficking, safety), engagement, grievance/remedy, actions and effectiveness, targets, workforce characteristics (employees and non-employees), collective bargaining, diversity, adequate wages, social protection, disability inclusion, training, H&S metrics (accidents, fatalities, lost days), work-life balance, remuneration metrics (gender pay gap, CEO pay ratio). S1-17 (incidents, severe human rights impacts) marked not material.
    - S2 (Workers in the value chain): Stakeholder views; policies and commitments, OECD/UNGP alignment; remediation channels; actions and effectiveness; risks of child/forced labor; minimum disclosures.
    - S3 (Affected communities): Policies and commitments; remedy channels; actions and effectiveness; minimum disclosures.
    - S4 (Consumers and end-users): Policies; engagement and remedy channels; actions and effectiveness; targets; minimum disclosures.
  - Governance (G1): Business conduct policies and culture (UN Anti-Corruption Convention, whistleblower protection); supplier relationship management; corruption/bribery prevention and detection; resilience; minimum disclosures. G1-4 (incidents of corruption/bribery) marked not material.
  - Additional topics with minimum disclosures: Meaningful Investment/Financing/Insurance; Information security & data protection; Financial inclusion; Innovation & digitalization; Resilience.

- EU Taxonomy mandatory disclosures:
  - Data quality caveat: Counterparty-reported data remain incomplete/inaccurate in year two; Belfius performed manual checks but accuracy depends on counterparties, highlighting persistent data availability/reliability challenges.
  - Consolidated KPIs: Weighted average Taxonomy-aligned KPIs across business segments (turnover- and CapEx-based). Reported totals: revenue EUR 3,140m; average KPI 0.23% (turnover-based) and 0.33% (CapEx-based). Note that the non-life underwriting KPI is not turnover or CapEx-based.

- Belfius as a credit institution (Annex VI & XII of Disclosure Delegated Act):
  - Mandatory templates cover Green Asset Ratio (GAR) and off-balance sheet exposures; separate nuclear and fossil gas templates (Annex XII) where relevant.
  - Scope: Prudential consolidation per CRR (EU 575/2013). GAR includes on-balance sheet exposures (loans/advances, debt securities, equities, repossessed collateral). Off-balance sheet covers financial guarantees and assets under management.
  - Methodological note: Totals use FINREP gross carrying amounts; differences may arise versus Annex VI templates due to FINREP being based on accounting categories rather than prudential banking/trading book concepts.

nodes.summary:
- Context: Part of Belfius Bank’s 2024 Annual Report Sustainability Statement detailing EU Taxonomy mandatory disclosures (Section 5.2).
- Data quality caveat: Belfius notes ongoing challenges with counterparties’ data availability and accuracy; despite manual quality checks, reporting depends on client/investee information.
- Consolidated Taxonomy KPIs: Belfius publishes a weighted average of Taxonomy-aligned KPIs across business segments, as requested by the European Commission.
  - Segments covered: banking activities, asset management (within Belfius Bank and Belfius Asset Management), insurance investment activities, and non-life insurance.
  - Overall weighted averages: Turnover-based KPI ≈ 0.23%; CapEx-based KPI ≈ 0.33%.
  - Indicative segment insights: banking accounts for ~76% of revenue with low alignment (~0.12–0.15%); insurance investment activities show comparatively higher alignment (~0.82–1.24%); asset management segments are small with low-to-moderate alignment; non-life insurance underwriting KPI is not turnover or CapEx-based (not comparable).
- Credit institution disclosures (Section 5.2.1):
  - Mandatory templates: Annex VI (core credit institution templates) and Annex XII (nuclear and fossil gas-related activities) of the Disclosure Delegated Act; guidance per Annex V.
  - Metrics disclosed: Green Asset Ratio (GAR) for on-balance sheet exposures and a KPI for off-balance sheet exposures.
  - Scope and methodology: Based on Belfius Bank’s prudential consolidation under CRR (Regulation (EU) No 575/2013); GAR covers loans and advances, debt securities, equity instruments, and repossessed collateral; off-balance sheet covers financial guarantees and assets under management.
  - Data basis: Totals computed from gross carrying amounts under FINREP; possible discrepancies with prudential views (banking vs trading book) due to differing accounting vs prudential categorizations.

nodes.title: Consolidated KPIs
nodes.heading: Consolidated KPIs
nodes.start_phrase: As requested by the European Commission, Belfius publishes a computation of the weighted average of KPIs on Taxonomy -aligned activities.
nodes.summary:
- Presents Belfius Bank’s mandatory EU Taxonomy disclosures for 2024, including required templates.
- Notes this is the second year of Taxonomy alignment reporting and highlights ongoing data availability and reliability challenges due to counterparty reporting; Belfius performed manual checks but depends on client/investee data.
- Provides consolidated KPIs across business segments with a weighted average of Taxonomy-aligned activities, as requested by the European Commission:
  - Total group revenue: EUR 3,140 million.
  - Weighted average KPIs: 0.23% (turnover-based) and 0.33% (CapEx-based).
  - Segments covered: Banking, Asset Management (Belfius Bank and Belfius Asset Management), Investments (Belfius Insurance), and Non-life Insurance (note: underwriting KPI is not turnover- or CapEx-based).
- Introduces credit institution disclosures (Annex VI & Annex XII of the Disclosure Delegated Act):
  - Presents the Green Asset Ratio (GAR) and KPI on off-balance sheet exposures.
  - Reporting follows Annex V guidance and Annex VI templates; nuclear and fossil gas-related activities are disclosed per Annex XII.
- Defines scope and methodology:
  - Based on Belfius Bank’s prudential consolidation per Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 (CRR).
  - GAR covers on-balance sheet exposures: loans and advances, debt securities, equity instruments, and repossessed collateral; off-balance sheet exposures include financial guarantees and assets under management.
  - Total assets in Annex VI templates use FINREP gross carrying amounts; due to differences between FINREP accounting categories and prudential banking/trading book concepts, totals may not align perfectly across reports.
