nodes.summary:
- Presents Belfius Bank’s mandatory EU Taxonomy disclosures for 2024, noting this is the second year of alignment reporting and highlighting persistent data availability and reliability gaps from counterparties despite Belfius’ manual quality checks.
- Provides consolidated Taxonomy KPIs across business segments, including revenue shares, segment-level turnover- and CapEx-based KPIs, and their weighted contributions:
  - Banking activities: EUR 2,398m (76.36%); KPI Turnover 0.12%, CapEx 0.15% (weighted 0.10%, 0.12%).
  - Asset management (Belfius Bank): EUR 109m (3.69%); KPI Turnover 0.01%, CapEx 0.16% (weighted 0.00%, 0.01%).
  - Asset management (Belfius Asset Management): EUR 56m (1.90%); KPI Turnover 0.92%, CapEx 1.26% (weighted 0.02%, 0.02%).
  - Investments (Belfius Insurance): EUR 480m (15.29%); KPI Turnover 0.82%, CapEx 1.24% (weighted 0.13%, 0.19%).
  - Non-life insurance: EUR 97m (3.09%); shown as 0.00% in the turnover/capex columns; note that the underwriting KPI for non-life is not turnover- or CapEx-based.
  - Group weighted averages: KPI Turnover 0.23%, KPI CapEx 0.33%.
- Details 5.2.1 (credit institution disclosures): Belfius reports its Green Asset Ratio (GAR) and KPI on off-balance sheet exposures per the Disclosure Delegated Act (Annex V guidance; Annex VI templates; Annex XII for nuclear and fossil gas-related activities).
- Defines scope and methodology: based on prudential consolidation under CRR (Regulation (EU) No 575/2013); GAR covers loans and advances, debt securities, equity instruments, and repossessed collaterals; off-balance sheet exposures include financial guarantees and assets under management.
- Explains that totals in Annex VI are computed using FINREP gross carrying amounts; due to differences between accounting categories (FINREP) and prudential concepts (banking vs trading book), figures may not align perfectly across templates.

nodes.title: Scope of assets and activities
nodes.heading: Scope of assets and activities
nodes.start_phrase: The EU Taxonomy disclosures are based on Belfius Bank’s scope of prudential consolidation determined in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, Title II, Chapter 2, Section 2.
nodes.summary:
- Presents Belfius Bank’s mandatory EU Taxonomy disclosures for 2024, including consolidated KPIs and credit institution templates per the Disclosure Delegated Act (Annex VI; Annex XII for nuclear and fossil gas).
- Highlights ongoing data availability and reliability challenges; disclosures depend on counterparties’ information despite Belfius’s manual quality checks.
- Provides consolidated, segment-level KPIs for Taxonomy-aligned activities with revenue weights:
  - Banking, asset management (Bank and Belfius Asset Management), investments (Belfius Insurance), and non-life insurance.
  - Shows very low weighted averages of Taxonomy-aligned KPIs: Turnover-based 0.23% and CapEx-based 0.33%; notes that non-life underwriting KPIs are not turnover or CapEx-based.
- Details scope and methodology for the Green Asset Ratio (GAR) and off-balance sheet KPIs:
  - Based on prudential consolidation (CRR 575/2013).
  - On-balance coverage includes loans and advances, debt securities, equity instruments, and repossessed collateral.
  - Off-balance covers financial guarantees and assets under management, with Belfius Asset Management’s AUM excluded from the credit institution KPI to avoid double counting.
  - Notes possible differences between FINREP totals and Annex VI totals due to differing bases (accounting vs prudential).
- Explains data sources and limitations:
  - Flow coverage not reported because new exposures to central governments, supranationals, and central banks cannot be isolated; otherwise would misleadingly show 100% coverage.
  - T-1 figures use Pillar III ESG data as of 31 Dec 2023 to reflect minor recalculations and ensure comparability.
- Mortgages: largest “use of proceeds” share is residential real estate, but no mortgage exposures are considered Taxonomy-aligned due to inability to evidence DNSH—especially physical risk assessment for climate change adaptation—across all loans.
- Local governments: no eligible exposures identified; social housing is financed by Regions (not local governments per NBB), and local entities cannot yet evidence full Taxonomy alignment.
- GAR sector information is based on counterparties’ main NACE codes; potential inaccuracies in NACE coding affect reliability.
- Interprets the “[Gross] carrying amount” column as representing eligibility for alignment calculations.

nodes.title: Flow
nodes.heading: Flow
nodes.start_phrase: Regarding the summary of the GAR on flow, specifically the percentage of coverage, Belfius does not provide this information in Table 0.
nodes.summary:
- KPI on assets under management excludes Belfius Asset Management exposures to avoid double counting, as these are reported separately under Annex IV of the Disclosure Delegated Act.
- Data sources and limitations (Flow/GAR): Belfius does not disclose the percentage coverage in Table 0 because it cannot isolate new exposures to central governments, supranationals, and central banks; a default 100% coverage would be misleading.
- T-1 figures: Use Pillar III ESG disclosures as of 31 December 2023 (not the 2023 Sustainability Report) to reflect minor recalculations and ensure consistency with current-year figures.
- Mortgages: Residential real estate is the largest known use-of-proceeds activity. Belfius cannot currently evidence DNSH criteria—especially physical risk assessment for climate change adaptation—so no mortgage loans are classified as EU Taxonomy-aligned.
- Local governments: No eligible activities identified. Social housing is financed by Belgian Regions (not “local governments” per the National Bank of Belgium), and local governments lack sufficient evidence to prove Taxonomy alignment.
- GAR sector information: Based on counterparties’ main NACE-coded activity only; potential code inaccuracies may affect reliability. The “Gross carrying amount” column is interpreted as the eligibility amount used for alignment assessment under each objective.

nodes.title: T-1 figures
nodes.heading: T-1 figures
nodes.start_phrase: The "T -1" figures refer to those reported in the Pillar III ESG disclosures as of 31 December 2023, rather than those published in the 2023 Sustainability Report.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and methodology notes for EU Taxonomy/Green Asset Ratio (GAR) reporting in Belfius Bank’s 2024 Annual Report Sustainability Statement.
- KPI on assets under management excludes Belfius Asset Management exposures to avoid double counting, since these are reported separately under Annex IV of the Disclosure Delegated Act.
- Data sources and limitations:
  - GAR “flow” coverage is not disclosed in Table 0 because Belfius cannot isolate new exposures to central governments, supranationals, and central banks; otherwise coverage appears falsely as 100%.
  - “T-1” figures are taken from Pillar III ESG disclosures as of 31 Dec 2023 (not the 2023 Sustainability Report) to reflect minor recalculations and ensure year-over-year comparability.
- Mortgages: Residential real estate is the largest known use-of-proceeds activity, but Belfius does not classify any mortgage loans as EU Taxonomy-aligned due to challenges proving DNSH (especially physical risk assessment for climate change adaptation) and the requirement that all technical screening criteria be met and evidenced.
- Local governments: No eligible activities identified, largely because Belgian social housing is financed by Regions (not counted as local governments) and current lack of sufficient alignment evidence from local governments.
- GAR sector information relies on counterparties’ main NACE codes where eligible exposures exist; potential inaccuracies in codes may affect reporting reliability.
- “[Gross] carrying amount” is interpreted as the eligibility measure and is presented under each relevant objective for alignment purposes.

- Explains Belfius’ EU Taxonomy/GAR reporting scope and methodology, notably excluding Belfius Asset Management assets from the KPI to avoid double counting (these are reported under Annex IV for asset managers).
- Details data limitations: Belfius does not disclose the flow GAR coverage percentage in Table 0 because it cannot isolate new exposures to central governments, supranationals, and central banks; doing so would misleadingly show 100% coverage.
- Clarifies that T-1 figures are sourced from the Pillar III ESG disclosures as of 31 December 2023 (not the 2023 Sustainability Report) to reflect minor recalculations and ensure comparability.
- Mortgages: While residential real estate is the largest “known use of proceeds” activity, Belfius does not classify any mortgage loans as EU Taxonomy-aligned due to inability to fully evidence DNSH criteria, particularly physical risk assessments for climate adaptation.
- Local governments: No eligible exposures identified; social housing is financed by Regions (not local governments per the NBB), and local authorities currently cannot provide full evidence of Taxonomy alignment.
- GAR sector information relies on counterparties’ main NACE codes for eligible exposures; potential inaccuracies in codes may affect reporting reliability.
- Interprets the “[Gross] carrying amount” column as the eligibility amount used for alignment calculations under each relevant objective.

nodes.title: Local governments
nodes.heading: Local governments
nodes.start_phrase: No exposure to eligible activities towards local governments is identified.
nodes.summary:
- Context: Extract from Belfius Bank’s 2024 Annual Report (Management Report – Sustainability Statement) detailing EU Taxonomy and Green Asset Ratio (GAR) disclosures, data sources, and limitations.
- KPI on assets under management: Exposures managed by Belfius Asset Management are reported separately under Annex IV of the Disclosure Delegated Act and excluded from the bank’s KPI to avoid double counting.
- Data sources and limitations (Flow): Belfius does not disclose the GAR flow coverage percentage in Table 0 because it cannot isolate new exposures to central governments, supranational issuers, and central banks; including them would incorrectly imply 100% coverage.
- T-1 figures: Prior-year (T-1) data are taken from Pillar III ESG disclosures as of 31 December 2023, not from the 2023 Sustainability Report, to reflect minor post-publication adjustments and ensure consistency and comparability.
- Mortgages: The main known use-of-proceeds activity is residential real estate. Belfius cannot currently demonstrate full EU Taxonomy alignment due to complex DNSH requirements—especially verifying physical climate risks for the adaptation objective—so no mortgage loans are counted as aligned.
- Local governments: No eligible exposures identified. Social housing is financed by Belgian Regions (not classified as local governments by the National Bank of Belgium), and local governments cannot yet provide full evidence of Taxonomy alignment.
- GAR sector information: Reporting relies on counterparties’ main NACE codes for eligible exposures; potential errors/inaccuracies in codes affect reliability. Belfius interprets the “[Gross] carrying amount” column as representing eligibility data used for alignment and shown under each relevant objective.

nodes.title: GAR sector information
nodes.heading: GAR sector information
nodes.start_phrase: The GAR sector information is limited to the main activity of Belfius’ counterparties and is exclusively based on the NACE codes for which Belfius has eligible exposures.
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: EU Taxonomy Article 8 disclosures for Belfius Bank (2024), focusing on mandatory KPIs for credit institutions, notably the Green Asset Ratio (GAR), with comparative “T-1” figures taken from Pillar III ESG disclosures as of 31 December 2023 to ensure consistency after minor post-publication adjustments.

- Methodology and boundaries:
  - Assets under management (AuM) of Belfius Asset Management are reported via the asset manager template (Annex IV) and excluded from bank KPIs to avoid double counting.
  - GAR sector information is based on counterparties’ main NACE codes, which may contain inaccuracies; “[Gross] carrying amount” is interpreted as eligibility.
  - Flow GAR coverage is not disclosed: the bank cannot isolate new exposures to central governments, supranationals and central banks (which must be excluded from the base), leading otherwise to a misleading 100% coverage.
  - For general lending, the Turnover KPI is used; CapEx KPI applies except for general lending.

- Key limitations and alignment stance:
  - Mortgages: while residential real estate dominates known use-of-proceeds activities, Belfius cannot yet evidence DNSH (especially physical risk assessments for climate adaptation), so no mortgage loans are considered Taxonomy-aligned.
  - Local governments: no eligible exposures identified; Belgian social housing is financed at the Regional level (not “local governments” per NBB) and local entities cannot yet provide full alignment evidence.

- Main KPI outcomes (Table 0, 2024):
  - GAR (stock): €358.94m environmentally sustainable assets; 0.12% (Turnover) and 0.15% (CapEx); 78.59% coverage; with exclusions per Article 7 from numerator (41.31%) and denominator (21.41%).
  - GAR (flow): €31.64m; 0.08%–0.09% (coverage not shown due to data limitation).
  - Additional KPIs (selected): Financial guarantees €84.70m; AuM €170.17m; trading book KPI noted where applicable.

- Balance sheet and coverage (2024):
  - Total assets: €172.75bn; assets covered for GAR: €135.77bn; not covered: €36.98bn (of which central banks €22.05bn, central governments/supranationals €9.86bn, trading book €5.07bn).
  - Within covered assets, loans/debt/equity eligible for GAR: €64.41bn; Taxonomy-eligible exposures concentrated in households (€43.23bn, mostly residential mortgages €42.81bn) but with zero alignment recognized for mortgages; non-financial corporates show the bulk of aligned amounts.
  - Other environmental objectives (water, circular economy, pollution, biodiversity): negligible eligibility/alignment.

- Off-balance-sheet (2024, undertakings subject to NFRD):
  - Financial guarantees: €443.48m with limited aligned amounts.
  - AuM: €99.79bn with small Taxonomy-eligible/aligned portions; detailed splits between debt and equity provided.

- Comparative view (2023 vs 2024 extracts):
  - Similar template disclosures for 2023 show lower total assets (€165.33bn) and GAR-covered assets (€130.80bn).
  - Year-on-year shifts in eligible/aligned amounts within non-financial corporates and in off-balance AuM, reflecting methodology updates and market dynamics.

- Sectoral breakdown (Table 2, NACE 4-digit):
  - Eligible exposures mainly in electricity transmission/distribution and utility construction (F42.2.2), as well as electrical equipment manufacturing and postal services; selected amounts reported as environmentally sustainable for climate change mitigation where evidence supports alignment.
  - Disclosure limited to counterparties’ main activity codes; no alignment reported for water/marine, circular economy, pollution, or biodiversity in the sector table.

nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: EU Taxonomy Article 8 disclosures for Belfius Bank (2024), focusing on mandatory KPIs for credit institutions, notably the Green Asset Ratio (GAR), with comparative “T-1” figures taken from Pillar III ESG disclosures as of 31 December 2023 to ensure consistency after minor post-publication adjustments.

- Methodology and boundaries:
  - Assets under management (AuM) of Belfius Asset Management are reported via the asset manager template (Annex IV) and excluded from bank KPIs to avoid double counting.
  - GAR sector information is based on counterparties’ main NACE codes, which may contain inaccuracies; “[Gross] carrying amount” is interpreted as eligibility.
  - Flow GAR coverage is not disclosed: the bank cannot isolate new exposures to central governments, supranationals and central banks (which must be excluded from the base), leading otherwise to a misleading 100% coverage.
  - For general lending, the Turnover KPI is used; CapEx KPI applies except for general lending.

- Key limitations and alignment stance:
  - Mortgages: while residential real estate dominates known use-of-proceeds activities, Belfius cannot yet evidence DNSH (especially physical risk assessments for climate adaptation), so no mortgage loans are considered Taxonomy-aligned.
  - Local governments: no eligible exposures identified; Belgian social housing is financed at the Regional level (not “local governments” per NBB) and local entities cannot yet provide full alignment evidence.

- Main KPI outcomes (Table 0, 2024):
  - GAR (stock): €358.94m environmentally sustainable assets; 0.12% (Turnover) and 0.15% (CapEx); 78.59% coverage; with exclusions per Article 7 from numerator (41.31%) and denominator (21.41%).
  - GAR (flow): €31.64m; 0.08%–0.09% (coverage not shown due to data limitation).
  - Additional KPIs (selected): Financial guarantees €84.70m; AuM €170.17m; trading book KPI noted where applicable.

- Balance sheet and coverage (2024):
  - Total assets: €172.75bn; assets covered for GAR: €135.77bn; not covered: €36.98bn (of which central banks €22.05bn, central governments/supranationals €9.86bn, trading book €5.07bn).
  - Within covered assets, loans/debt/equity eligible for GAR: €64.41bn; Taxonomy-eligible exposures concentrated in households (€43.23bn, mostly residential mortgages €42.81bn) but with zero alignment recognized for mortgages; non-financial corporates show the bulk of aligned amounts.
  - Other environmental objectives (water, circular economy, pollution, biodiversity): negligible eligibility/alignment.

- Off-balance-sheet (2024, undertakings subject to NFRD):
  - Financial guarantees: €443.48m with limited aligned amounts.
  - AuM: €99.79bn with small Taxonomy-eligible/aligned portions; detailed splits between debt and equity provided.

- Comparative view (2023 vs 2024 extracts):
  - Similar template disclosures for 2023 show lower total assets (€165.33bn) and GAR-covered assets (€130.80bn).
  - Year-on-year shifts in eligible/aligned amounts within non-financial corporates and in off-balance AuM, reflecting methodology updates and market dynamics.

- Sectoral breakdown (Table 2, NACE 4-digit):
  - Eligible exposures mainly in electricity transmission/distribution and utility construction (F42.2.2), as well as electrical equipment manufacturing and postal services; selected amounts reported as environmentally sustainable for climate change mitigation where evidence supports alignment.
  - Disclosure limited to counterparties’ main activity codes; no alignment reported for water/marine, circular economy, pollution, or biodiversity in the sector table.

nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: EU Taxonomy Article 8 disclosures for Belfius Bank (2024), focusing on mandatory KPIs for credit institutions, notably the Green Asset Ratio (GAR), with comparative “T-1” figures taken from Pillar III ESG disclosures as of 31 December 2023 to ensure consistency after minor post-publication adjustments.

- Methodology and boundaries:
  - Assets under management (AuM) of Belfius Asset Management are reported via the asset manager template (Annex IV) and excluded from bank KPIs to avoid double counting.
  - GAR sector information is based on counterparties’ main NACE codes, which may contain inaccuracies; “[Gross] carrying amount” is interpreted as eligibility.
  - Flow GAR coverage is not disclosed: the bank cannot isolate new exposures to central governments, supranationals and central banks (which must be excluded from the base), leading otherwise to a misleading 100% coverage.
  - For general lending, the Turnover KPI is used; CapEx KPI applies except for general lending.

- Key limitations and alignment stance:
  - Mortgages: while residential real estate dominates known use-of-proceeds activities, Belfius cannot yet evidence DNSH (especially physical risk assessments for climate adaptation), so no mortgage loans are considered Taxonomy-aligned.
  - Local governments: no eligible exposures identified; Belgian social housing is financed at the Regional level (not “local governments” per NBB) and local entities cannot yet provide full alignment evidence.

- Main KPI outcomes (Table 0, 2024):
  - GAR (stock): €358.94m environmentally sustainable assets; 0.12% (Turnover) and 0.15% (CapEx); 78.59% coverage; with exclusions per Article 7 from numerator (41.31%) and denominator (21.41%).
  - GAR (flow): €31.64m; 0.08%–0.09% (coverage not shown due to data limitation).
  - Additional KPIs (selected): Financial guarantees €84.70m; AuM €170.17m; trading book KPI noted where applicable.

- Balance sheet and coverage (2024):
  - Total assets: €172.75bn; assets covered for GAR: €135.77bn; not covered: €36.98bn (of which central banks €22.05bn, central governments/supranationals €9.86bn, trading book €5.07bn).
  - Within covered assets, loans/debt/equity eligible for GAR: €64.41bn; Taxonomy-eligible exposures concentrated in households (€43.23bn, mostly residential mortgages €42.81bn) but with zero alignment recognized for mortgages; non-financial corporates show the bulk of aligned amounts.
  - Other environmental objectives (water, circular economy, pollution, biodiversity): negligible eligibility/alignment.

- Off-balance-sheet (2024, undertakings subject to NFRD):
  - Financial guarantees: €443.48m with limited aligned amounts.
  - AuM: €99.79bn with small Taxonomy-eligible/aligned portions; detailed splits between debt and equity provided.

- Comparative view (2023 vs 2024 extracts):
  - Similar template disclosures for 2023 show lower total assets (€165.33bn) and GAR-covered assets (€130.80bn).
  - Year-on-year shifts in eligible/aligned amounts within non-financial corporates and in off-balance AuM, reflecting methodology updates and market dynamics.

- Sectoral breakdown (Table 2, NACE 4-digit):
  - Eligible exposures mainly in electricity transmission/distribution and utility construction (F42.2.2), as well as electrical equipment manufacturing and postal services; selected amounts reported as environmentally sustainable for climate change mitigation where evidence supports alignment.
  - Disclosure limited to counterparties’ main activity codes; no alignment reported for water/marine, circular economy, pollution, or biodiversity in the sector table.

- Scope and frameworks: Belfius Insurance reports on how its underwriting portfolio contributes to the EU Taxonomy objective of climate change adaptation and how its investment portfolio relates to all environmental objectives, following Annex IX guidelines and Annex X templates of the Disclosure Delegated Act; nuclear and fossil gas information follows Annex XII templates.

- Underwriting scope: Only two non-life lines cover climate-related perils—other motor insurance (casco) and fire and other damage to property.

- Investment scope: All direct and indirect investments are included (collective investment undertakings, participations, loans, mortgages, and property).

- Underwriting KPI methodology and results:
  - Six-step approach: calculate total non-life GWP (12 Solvency II LOBs); identify LOBs covering climate perils; compute the proportion of premiums eligible at peril level; then assess Taxonomy alignment (steps 4–6).
  - Method refinement: FY2021–FY2022 considered full GWP of relevant LOBs as eligible; from FY2023, detailed peril-level calculations are applied.
  - Eligibility outcome: 12.13% of premiums are Taxonomy-eligible at consolidated level.
  - Alignment assessment: Based on five tiers—leadership in climate risk modelling/pricing, product design, innovative coverage, data sharing, and post-disaster service levels. Current alignment is 0% due to not yet meeting the forward-looking pricing model requirement; sector guidance on forward-looking scenarios is pending.
  - DNSH and MSS: DNSH screened contract-by-contract to exclude activities linked to fossil fuels, affecting <0.06% of premiums; MSS reinforced through a revised Human Rights Policy. Further methodology refinements planned as guidance evolves.

- Investment KPI methodology and limitations:
  - Relies on investee disclosures of Taxonomy eligibility/alignment via ESG data providers.
  - For unit-linked (Branche 23) life products, EET files used for SFDR lack eligibility data; these are reported as 0% eligible and 0% aligned to avoid estimates. Alternatives to obtain eligibility data are being explored.

nodes.summary:
- Section of Belfius Bank’s 2024 Management Report – Sustainability Statement presenting EU Taxonomy disclosures for turnover and CAPEX.
- Focus on amounts and proportions of taxonomy-eligible but not taxonomy-aligned economic activities included in the denominator of the applicable KPIs, broken down by climate objectives:
  - Climate change mitigation (CCM)
  - Climate change adaptation (CCA)
- Detailed breakdown by EU Taxonomy Delegated Regulation 2021/2139, Annexes I and II, Sections 4.26 to 4.31, plus an “other taxonomy-eligible” category.
- Key totals reported:
  - Turnover (eligible but not aligned): 131.11 (0.36%), of which CCM 116.64 (0.32%) and CCA 14.47 (0.04%).
  - CAPEX (eligible but not aligned): 422.38 (1.17%), of which CCM 348.90 (0.97%) and CCA 73.48 (0.20%).
- Section-level highlights (amounts; all percentages ~0.00–0.01%):
  - 4.26: 0.00 (turnover and CAPEX).
  - 4.27: CAPEX 0.05.
  - 4.28: Turnover 0.01; CAPEX 0.02.
  - 4.29: Turnover 1.50; CAPEX 1.82 (including CCM 0.91).
  - 4.30: Turnover 0.90; CAPEX 0.22 (including CCM 0.13).
  - 4.31: Turnover 0.13; CAPEX 0.09.
  - “Other taxonomy-eligible” is the dominant share: Turnover 128.57 (CCM 114.10; CCA 14.47); CAPEX 420.18 (CCM 347.86; CCA 73.48).
- Separate “Table 5 – Taxonomy not eligible economic activities” shows no amounts reported (all entries marked “-”) for both turnover and CAPEX, indicating no disclosure of taxonomy-non-eligible activities in this extract.
